items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear and there is a comment on the re-parse branch. But f-strings (f"{auth}@{netloc}") break the codebase's .format/join idiom, the tuple unpacking is repeated, and removing `return auth` left an extra blank line in get_auth_from_url.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Goes well past the needed fix: edits adapters.py, rebuild_proxies (now uses select_proxy), and get_auth_from_url, which now calls prepend_scheme_if_needed. prepend_scheme_if_needed parses twice and repeats the unpack line. Adds coupling and scope creep the issue didn't need.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: f-strings are a SyntaxError on Python 2.7, which requests 2.27 still supported. The `url.startswith(f"{scheme}://")` check fails for uppercase schemes because parse_url lowercases them, so 'HTTP://h' is re-parsed as 'http://HTTP://h'. Still catches broad (AttributeError, TypeError) and returns ('','').

items.name: prepend_scheme_if_needed public behaviour unchanged otherwise
items.name_zh: prepend_scheme_if_needed 其他公开行为不变
items.evidence: No-auth behaviour changed: new `if not url: return url` early exit, and a re-parse with new_scheme prepended whenever the parsed scheme doesn't literally prefix the URL, which breaks uppercase-scheme URLs. get_auth_from_url semantics also changed (user-only now returns ('user','')). Far more than re-attaching auth.
